chapter: Image, travel and Black, Brown and Beige
title: Appearance is half the battle: uniforms and his teacher's advice
summary: Irving Mills and Duke insisted on looking sharp; changed uniforms each show.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Oh, I know what I wanted to ask you. Did you have -- at that time, too, do you think that's one of the reasons, given those kinds of pressures, are you saying that's one of the reasons why the guys -- like you were talking earlier about how the guys always are involved with dignity and having their presentations be real exact, everything on the button, guys look good, clean-shaven, you know, have their music down, have all their music memorized and everything, that that was a way of making sure that --

Yeah, well, you see, our manager, Irvin Mills, and Duke, insisted that we look good. We were the most dressed up band in the world. We did four or five shows a day, sometimes six, at a theater, each show we changed complete, from head to toe, uniforms. Everytime we played Carnegie Hall or important on that status (gible), He would have the tailor make us complete uniforms, complete shoes, everything. Because he always -- Irving Mills was a very shrewd man. And he knew appearance was half the battle. When you look good, and can play good, you can't miss.

Well, I've seen photographs of you all in Washington in the twenties before you all even met Irving Mills, and seen that you and Ellington and Hardwick were pretty sharp, about as sharp as you can get.

You see, when I went to school one of the main things my teacher, German lady, insisted on, now, a lot of you are going to be professional musicians. She'd say, "Well, let me tell you something." She's a German lady. "She'd say, appearance is half the battle. Always look good. If you look good and can play good, you can't miss."

What did she say that for, man. I became a clothes horse, you know. I was dressing sharp. That's one reason why I became a drummer. I saw this cat, Peg ? , man, he was a Rembrandt picture. He was tall and elegant. I said, "Man, I'd like to look like that." That was sharp as -- oeee, he was a gasser! I never seen -- sharp on the stage, off the stage. This cat, I said, yeah, that's it. I'm going to be like that one day, I'm going to be like that. And that was it.
